ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows two cascaded ideal inverting operational amplifier stages. The non-inverting terminal of the first stage is grounded, the input signal is labeled Vs=10cos(100t), connected to the inverting terminal through a 10Ω resistor, and the feedback element is an inductor labeled 10mH, feeding back from the first-stage output to the inverting terminal. The non-inverting terminal of the second stage is also grounded, the first-stage output is connected to the second-stage inverting terminal through a 100Ω resistor, and the feedback element is a capacitor labeled 10μF; the second-stage output is labeled Vo. Reasoning: Convert the input Vs=10cos(100t) to a phasor, Vs=10∠0, angular frequency ω=100 rad/s. The first stage is an inverting structure, gain V1/Vs = -Zf/Zin = -jωL/R = -j(100)(0.01)/10 = -j0.1, therefore V1 = (-j0.1)(10) = -j. The second stage is also an inverting structure, the feedback impedance is the capacitor impedance 1/(jωC), and the input resistance is 100Ω, so Vo/V1 = -[1/(jωC)]/100 = -1/[j(100)(10μF)(100)] = +j10. The total gain is (-j0.1)(j10)=1, so the output and input have the same amplitude and the same phase. Therefore Vo=10cos(100t).
